title: Design a research schema for mapping online earning mechanisms
priority_reason: The company needs a uniform record so that agents do not collect random ideas without comparable evidence.
summary: Define the minimal fields for a mechanism scan: offer, customer, channel, evidence, risks, ToS/legal notes, cost estimate, first experiment and sources with a verification date.
risk_notes: Research must not copy another company's brand, databases, customer data or non-public know-how.
Online market data goes stale quickly; every scan must have a verification date and links to sources.
acceptance_criteria: There is a proposed JSON/Markdown template for one mechanism scan.
The template contains a guardrail section and fields for sources.
It is clear whether the first version belongs in the root task ledger or in a future `workspace/research/`.

title: Create a longlist of existing online projects with verifiable income
priority_reason: The first research step should find real projects that already make money, so that the company does not plan on assumptions or viral claims without proof.
summary: Find 25-40 existing online projects, products, agencies, solo operators or agent-enabled companies that publicly show a monetization signal: revenue/MRR, prices, paid products, clients, marketplace sales, case studies, public accounting/traffic signals or other verifiable evidence. For every candidate, record the source, the verification date, the type of evidence, a short mechanism and a first estimate of whether the mechanism can be adapted for the company.
risk_notes: Do not copy another company's brand, content, databases, customer data, non-public know-how or identity; study only the mechanism and the legal adaptation.
Revenue claims may be outdated or embellished; every candidate must have a source, a verification date and a confidence level.
Do not use scraping, spam, fake engagement or ToS workarounds as part of a proposed mechanism.
acceptance_criteria: There is a longlist of at least 25 candidates with links to sources and a verification date.
Every candidate has a recorded monetization signal, mechanism, target customer, channel and confidence level.
The candidates are grouped into categories by mechanism type, for example lead-gen, micro-SaaS, content-to-service, marketplace arbitrage, agent services or data product.
Every candidate has a note on what the company may legally adapt and what it must not copy.

title: Narrow the longlist to mechanisms suitable for legal adaptation
priority_reason: The company needs to separate interesting stories quickly from mechanisms that can really be repeated with our resources, our agent advantage and reputational safety.
summary: The longlist was narrowed by scoring 10 candidates on revenue evidence, time-to-first-dollar, agent leverage, distribution availability, risks and delivery margin. Recommendation: Agent Automation Desk as the first test; the white-label AI support agent and the AI visibility audit as the next candidates.
risk_notes: A mechanism with a high revenue signal may be unsuitable if it rests on trust, a brand, capital, an audience or data that the company does not have.
Do not move a candidate to the shortlist if its main advantage rests on deception, platform spam or hard-to-defend imitation.
Scoring should separate verified evidence from hypotheses; viral popularity alone is not evidence of monetization.
acceptance_criteria: There is a scoring table or a JSON/Markdown record with criteria and weights.
There is a shortlist of 8-12 candidates with the highest potential for the company.
There is a reject/parking list with clear reasons for postponing.
The top candidates have their biggest risk and their fastest possible test marked.
next_action: Review the scoring and adjust the weights if needed before the next research iteration.

title: Break the top candidates down into a copyable mechanism without copying identity
priority_reason: The company's goal is not to copy someone else's surface but to understand the money mechanism and design its own version that can work legally and with an agent advantage.
summary: The top candidates were broken down at the level of the mechanism and the company's legal adaptation. Agent Automation Desk has a detailed experiment spec; the white-label AI support agent and the AI visibility audit have experiment cards and reasons for postponing.
risk_notes: The analysis must not become a guide to violating copyright, ToS, trademarks, privacy or customer trust.
Do not mistake a project's visible frontend for its real economic engine; for every candidate, find out exactly where the money is made.
In regulated or highly sensitive fields, mark the legal uncertainty instead of giving false certainty.
acceptance_criteria: Every deep dive has a structured breakdown: customer, offer, channel, pricing, delivery, evidence, risks, adaptation and first test.
Every candidate has a named version for the company that does not copy someone else's identity.
Every candidate has an explicit verdict: test now, postpone or drop.
At least three candidates have enough signal for an experiment proposal.
next_action: After the review, add a deeper deep dive for the second and third candidates if the first pilot gets no signal.

title: Prepare a shortlist of the first monetization experiments
priority_reason: Research should end quickly in a market test; the experiment shortlist connects the existing evidence with a concrete first step for the company.
summary: A shortlist of the first monetization experiments was created with three experiment cards and a clear recommendation for the first test. Agent Automation Desk is prepared as a spec waiting for human approval. An offer draft, outreach drafts, a discovery script, an intake template and a run log template are also prepared.
risk_notes: An experiment card must not start external actions automatically; starting a test requires explicit human confirmation.
Do not start an experiment until it is clear how a signal of interest, income or qualified demand will be recognized.
Prefer small tests with a reputationally safe output over aggressive distribution.
acceptance_criteria: There are 3-5 experiment cards ready for a decision.
Every experiment has a metric, a minimum budget, a stop condition and an expected time to the first signal.
One first experiment is recommended, with an explanation of why it has the best balance of speed, evidence and risk.
It is clear which steps an agent may take locally and which wait for human confirmation.
next_action: Alex is to approve the launch: the pilot price, ICP, prospect list and outreach message.

title: Set up Mission Control as the local planning layer of Lazurio Example Organization
priority_reason: The company needs a control-centre kind of planning place, but the data should be local YAML files in the workspace, so that agents work with them natively and without depending on an external task manager.
summary: Mission Control was chosen as the name and as the planned module `mission-control/`. The workspace rules describe the YAML-first planning model and the Mission Control plan -> TODO.tasks.json flow.
risk_notes: Mission Control must not introduce a second opaque database; the YAML files must stay authoritative.
No secrets, tokens, customer data or personal credentials may enter the plans.
The UI must not be the only source of truth; agents must be able to read and edit a plan as an ordinary file.
acceptance_criteria: The manifest contains the planned slot `mission-control/`.
The root rules say that new feature plans belong in Mission Control.
The skill `mission-control-planning` exists for turning a plan into implementation TODOs.
A reference model exists for YAML feature plans and their mapping to `TODO.tasks.json`.
`check-workspace-tasks.mjs` validates the optional `planning` reference in a task.
The Guide lesson on the first piece of work explains Mission Control planning and TODO execution.
next_action: After confirmation, create `mission-control/` as a nested repo and create the first YAML schema + a local editor skeleton.

title: Prepare an experiment checklist for the first monetization test
priority_reason: The first test should be measurable, cheap and safe; without a checklist it is easy to slide into vague activity without evidence.
summary: The first experiment checklist was created in workspace/experiments/checklists/. The checklist defines the hypothesis, offer, ICP, metric, budget, stop/scale decision, reputational guardrails and evidence requirements for the first monetization test.
risk_notes: An experiment must not trigger spam, phishing, fake engagement, scraping against the ToS or misleading claims.
Actions that leave the local environment must be confirmed by a person in advance.
acceptance_criteria: The checklist is usable for the first manual test and the first agent test.
It contains an explicit stop/scale decision.
The experiment result has a clear place to be recorded.
next_action: Alex is to confirm that the checklist is enough as a gate before the Agent Automation Desk pilot starts.

title: Choose the first mechanism for a detailed breakdown
priority_reason: The company needs a first concrete learning loop, but the choice should come only after a minimal comparison of the options and risks.
summary: The first mechanism for a detailed breakdown is chosen: DesignJoy-for-automation adapted as Agent Automation Desk, a productized agent automation service with a single active request queue.
risk_notes: The choice must not rest on a viral claim alone; there must be verifiable evidence of demand or monetization.
The mechanism must be adaptable legally and in a reputationally safe way.
acceptance_criteria: Every candidate has a short model and risks.
The chosen candidate has a reason for the choice and a next step.
The candidates not chosen have recorded reasons for postponing.
next_action: Confirm the pilot price, ICP and first outreach scope before starting external actions.

title: Optimize the root entrypoints for Claude Code
priority_reason: Lazurio Example Organization already has a shared `.claude/skills` library, a Codex symlink `.agents/skills` and a root `AGENTS.md` written so that Claude Code reads it too. What was missing was a native root entrypoint `CLAUDE.md`.
summary: Added a native `CLAUDE.md` and aligned the documentation and doctor checks so that Claude Code uses the same GEN2 cascade as Codex without a second copy of the rules.
risk_notes: Do not create a second long set of rules outside `AGENTS.md`.
Do not move secrets or per-person Claude settings into Git.
Do not mix this change with the Launchpad Claude backend.
acceptance_criteria: `CLAUDE.md` exists and points to `AGENTS.md` as the authoritative manual.
The root docs and `.claude/README.md` describe `CLAUDE.md` as an adapter, not a new source of truth.
The doctor check guards `CLAUDE.md` in both the shell and the PowerShell variant.
Guide lesson 11 is corrected for Lazurio Example Organization and explains when to use Claude Code.
Validation confirms the JSON/YAML syntax, the doctor check and the guide build.
next_action: Review the diff and, after approval, publish the super-repo and Mission Control plan changes through a pull request from a worktree.

title: Add the export of a Mission Control plan to TODO.tasks.json
priority_reason: Mission Control should hold the planning context, but implementation work should arise as concrete tasks in the Git-native task ledger.
summary: Design and implement the first safe export or proposal generator that prepares task items from a YAML plan for the nearest TODO.tasks.json.
risk_notes: The export must not overwrite existing tasks without explicit approval.
A plan may contain strategic context; the TODO should hold only concrete implementation steps.
acceptance_criteria: There is a proposed mapping from plan YAML to TODO.tasks.json.
The export has a dry-run mode.
The output contains a `planning` reference back to the YAML plan.

title: Design a Linear-like filesystem DB core for Mission Control
priority_reason: Mission Control should take over Linear's core workflow but keep the data as YAML files in the Git workspace, so that agents can work with them natively.
summary: Prepare the first architecture and schema for the Mission Control core entities: issues, projects, initiatives, cycles, triage, labels, views, workflows and updates. The result should be a simple filesystem DB contract that both the UI and agents can read.
risk_notes: Do not copy Linear's brand, UI texts, design or cloud architecture.
Views must not materialize copies of data; they should be stored filters over YAML entities.
The core model must not bypass the current validation or the safe bridge to `TODO.tasks.json`.
acceptance_criteria: There is a documented mapping of Linear-like concepts to Mission Control YAML entities.
A target folder structure for the filesystem DB is designed.
The V1/V2 boundary between the current `plans/` model and the future `issues/projects` core is clear.
There is a proposal for the first schemas for issue, project, initiative, workflow and view.

title: Evaluate the Mission Control dogfood planning loop
priority_reason: We are testing Mission Control by planning the further development of Mission Control in it. The goal is to walk the whole loop: a plan is created as YAML, the plan contains decisions and proposed tasks, the export creates implemen…
summary: Walk through plan -> export -> TODO -> evidence back and record which parts run smoothly and which slow agents down.
risk_notes: The dogfood must not bypass its own rules; tasks must come from the Mission Control export, not just from manual entries.
If the workflow turns out to be uncomfortable, that is a valid test result and should be recorded as friction, not hidden.
Do not plan the company's business strategy until the planning core is stable enough to capture decisions.
acceptance_criteria: What worked in the plan -> TODO flow is described.
What needed manual intervention outside the UI or API is described.
There is a recommendation for the next Mission Control improvement.

title: Add the missing editor field for decisions
priority_reason: We are testing Mission Control by planning the further development of Mission Control in it. The goal is to walk the whole loop: a plan is created as YAML, the plan contains decisions and proposed tasks, the export creates implemen…
summary: The UI detail already shows decisions, but the edit modal cannot edit them comfortably; add a minimal text field or a YAML-friendly editor pattern.
risk_notes: The dogfood must not bypass its own rules; tasks must come from the Mission Control export, not just from manual entries.
If the workflow turns out to be uncomfortable, that is a valid test result and should be recorded as friction, not hidden.
Do not plan the company's business strategy until the planning core is stable enough to capture decisions.
acceptance_criteria: An agent or a person can add a decision with a date and a rationale through the UI.
Saving keeps the YAML schema valid.
The existing plans UI stays functional.

title: Bring the root-level Mission Control work board migration to a verified state
priority_reason: Mission Control should be a root-level control-plane repo and at the same time the main overview of planned agent work over the filesystem ledgers.
summary: Finish moving Mission Control to the root-level repo, add the work board over the task ledgers, update the references and verify the Launchpad smoke test.
risk_notes: The super-repo must not start tracking the nested repo's content or a gitlink pointer.
The ledger scanner must not walk build/cache/runtime folders.
Older TODO tasks without Mission Control plans should first be made visible, not silently rewritten.
acceptance_criteria: Launchpad discovers Mission Control from the root-level manifest slot.
The work board API returns TODO/DONE/ISSUES columns.
The UI shows planning coverage and links to the plans.
The build, the registry tests and the workspace task validation pass.
